pellegrino-artusi.name: Pellegrino Artusi
pellegrino-artusi.summary: Italian businessman and writer (1820–1911) best known for his 1891 cookbook Science in the Kitchen and the Art of Eating Well.

victor-emmanuel-ii.name: Victor Emmanuel II
victor-emmanuel-ii.summary: King of Sardinia from 1849, who became the first king of a united Italy in 1861 and was called 'Father of the Fatherland'; he died in 1878.

napoleon.name: Napoleon
napoleon.summary: French emperor from 1804 to 1814, and briefly in 1815, who rose to power as a general during the French Revolution and led sweeping military campaigns across Europe and the Middle East.

pinzimonio.name: Pinzimonio
pinzimonio.summary: An Italian dipping sauce of olive oil, salt and pepper served cold with raw vegetables, especially popular around Rome and in Tuscany.

macchiaioli.name: Macchiaioli
macchiaioli.summary: Group of Italian painters active in Tuscany in the mid-to-late 19th century who painted outdoors to capture natural light, seen as forerunners of French Impressionism.

unification-of-italy.name: Risorgimento
unification-of-italy.summary: 19th-century political movement, also known as the unification of Italy, that led to the creation of the Kingdom of Italy in 1861, completed with Rome's designation as capital in 1871.

galleria-vittorio-emanuele-ii.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
galleria-vittorio-emanuele-ii.summary: Italy's oldest active shopping arcade, a four-story double gallery in central Milan named for King Victor Emmanuel II and built between 1865 and 1877.

galleria-umberto-i.name: Galleria Umberto I
galleria-umberto-i.summary: A grand shopping gallery in Naples built 1887–1890 during the city's post-cholera rebuilding, with a 57-metre glass dome; part of a UNESCO World Heritage site.

stile-umbertino.name: Stile Umbertino
stile-umbertino.summary: A 19th-century Italian Renaissance Revival style of architecture and decorative arts named after King Umberto I, most popular in Rome.

umberto-i-of-italy.name: Umberto I
umberto-i-of-italy.summary: King of Italy from 1878 until his assassination in 1900; his reign saw the creation of Italy's colonial empire and the Triple Alliance with Germany and Austria-Hungary.

eclecticism-in-art.name: Eclecticism
eclecticism-in-art.summary: An artistic approach that borrows and combines a variety of styles from different historical sources within a single work, rather than following one distinct style.

francesco-hayez.name: Francesco Hayez
francesco-hayez.summary: Italian painter (1791–1882) considered a leading artist of Romanticism in mid-19th-century Milan, known for grand historical paintings, political allegories and portraits.

the-kiss-hayez.name: The Kiss
the-kiss-hayez.summary: An 1859 painting by Francesco Hayez, probably his best-known work and an emblem of Italian Romanticism and the Risorgimento.

brera-academy.name: Brera Academy
brera-academy.summary: State-run academy of fine arts in Milan that shares its history and main building with the Pinacoteca di Brera, the city's main public art museum.

giovanni-fattori.name: Giovanni Fattori
giovanni-fattori.summary: Italian painter (1825–1908) and a leader of the Macchiaioli group, known for historical and military scenes and later landscapes inspired by the Barbizon school.

silvestro-lega.name: Silvestro Lega
silvestro-lega.summary: Italian realist painter, 1826–1895, one of the leading artists of the Macchiaioli and also involved with the Mazzini movement.

telemaco-signorini.name: Telemaco Signorini
telemaco-signorini.summary: Telemaco Signorini: Italian painter (1835–1901) who belonged to the Macchiaioli, a group of Italian artists.

porta-sempione.name: Arco della Pace
porta-sempione.summary: A 19th-century triumphal arch marking Milan's Porta Sempione gate, built on the site of an earlier gate in the city's Roman walls.

teatro-di-san-carlo.name: Teatro di San Carlo
teatro-di-san-carlo.summary: A historic opera house in Naples, opened in 1737, making it the oldest continuously active opera venue in the world and a model for later European theatres.

pedrocchi-caf.name: Pedrocchi Café
pedrocchi-caf.summary: An 18th-century café in central Padua, Italy, known for its eclectic architecture and its role in the 1848 riots against the Habsburg monarchy.

antonio-canova.name: Antonio Canova
antonio-canova.summary: Italian Neoclassical sculptor (1757–1822), often regarded as the greatest artist of the movement, famous for his marble sculptures.

accademia-di-belle-arti-di-venezia.name: Venice Academy
accademia-di-belle-arti-di-venezia.summary: A public academy of fine arts in Venice, Italy.
accademia-di-belle-arti-di-venezia.source_title: Accademia di Belle Arti di Venezia

venus-victrix-canova.name: Venus Victrix
venus-victrix-canova.summary: A neo-Classical marble sculpture of Pauline Bonaparte as the goddess Venus, made by Antonio Canova from 1805 to 1808 and now in Rome's Galleria Borghese.

pauline-bonaparte.name: Pauline Bonaparte
pauline-bonaparte.summary: Younger sister of Napoleon Bonaparte, an imperial French princess and Duchess of Guastalla who married French general Charles Leclerc and later Camillo Borghese, Prince of Sulmona.

renaissance-revival-architecture.name: Renaissance Revival architecture
renaissance-revival-architecture.summary: A group of 19th-century architectural styles that drew broadly on Renaissance forms rather than Greek or Gothic revival.

horatio-greenough.name: Horatio Greenough
horatio-greenough.summary: American sculptor (1805 to 1852) known for U.S. government commissions including The Rescue and a statue of George Washington.

william-wetmore-story.name: William Wetmore Story
william-wetmore-story.summary: An American sculptor, art critic, poet, and editor (1819–1895).

tommaso-minardi.name: Tommaso Minardi
tommaso-minardi.summary: Italian painter and art theorist (1787–1871) active in Rome and other cities, whose work moved from Neoclassicism toward Romanticism.

johann-friedrich-overbeck.name: Friedrich Overbeck
johann-friedrich-overbeck.summary: German painter (1789–1869) who founded the Nazarene art movement.

temporal-power-of-the-holy-see.name: Papal temporal power
temporal-power-of-the-holy-see.summary: The pope's rule over the Papal States in central Italy, distinct from spiritual authority, which ended in 1870 when Italian troops captured Rome.
temporal-power-of-the-holy-see.source_title: Temporal power of the Holy See

triple-alliance-1882.name: Triple Alliance (1882)
triple-alliance-1882.summary: A defensive alliance formed in 1882 between Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy, renewed periodically until 1915, though Italy ultimately fought World War I on the Allied side.

kingdom-of-sardinia-1720-1861.name: Kingdom of Sardinia (1720–1861)
kingdom-of-sardinia-1720-1861.summary: The Savoyard state ruling Sardinia and mainland territories like Savoy and Piedmont from 1720 to 1861, formed when Sardinia was ceded to the Duke of Savoy after Habsburg and Bourbon claims were settled.

second-italian-war-of-independence.name: Second Italian War of Independence
second-italian-war-of-independence.summary: An 1859 war in which France and the Kingdom of Sardinia defeated Austria, liberating Lombardy and advancing Italian unification.

plombi-res-agreement.name: Plombières Agreement
plombi-res-agreement.summary: A secret 1858 verbal pact between Piedmont-Sardinia's Cavour and France's Napoleon III that paved the way for war against Austria and Italian unification.

eight-nation-alliance.name: Eight-Nation Alliance
eight-nation-alliance.summary: A coalition of eight nations whose troops invaded northern China in 1900 to relieve besieged foreign legations during the Boxer Rebellion, later occupying and looting Beijing.

fasci-siciliani.name: Fasci Siciliani
fasci-siciliani.summary: A democratic and socialist popular movement that arose in Sicily between 1889 and 1894, crushed by the Italian government through harsh military repression in 1894.

francesco-crispi.name: Francesco Crispi
francesco-crispi.summary: Italian revolutionary and statesman who served four times as Prime Minister of Italy between 1887 and 1896, pursuing colonial expansion abroad while cracking down harshly on protest at home; the first Prime Minister from Southern Italy.

ni-ard-exodus.name: Niçard exodus
ni-ard-exodus.summary: The emigration of a quarter of the Niçard Italian population from Nice to Italy, after Nice's annexation to France in 1861.

giuseppe-garibaldi.name: Giuseppe Garibaldi
giuseppe-garibaldi.summary: An Italian general and revolutionary (1807–1882) central to Italy's unification, nicknamed the 'Hero of the Two Worlds' for campaigns in both South America and Europe.

ni-ard-vespers.name: Niçard Vespers
ni-ard-vespers.summary: Three days of popular uprising by the inhabitants of Nice in 1871, in support of uniting the County of Nice with the Kingdom of Italy.

italian-reformist-socialist-party.name: Italian Reformist Socialist Party
italian-reformist-socialist-party.summary: A social-democratic political party in Italy that broke away from the Italian Socialist Party.

italian-socialist-party.name: Italian Socialist Party
italian-socialist-party.summary: A social democratic party founded in Genoa in 1892, one of Italy's longest-surviving parties, which became Italy's leading political force by 1919.

sibilla-aleramo.name: Sibilla Aleramo
sibilla-aleramo.summary: Italian feminist writer and poet (1876-1960) known for autobiographical depictions of women's lives in late 19th-century Italy.

giacomo-leopardi.name: Giacomo Leopardi
giacomo-leopardi.summary: Italian poet and philosopher (1798 to 1837), considered the greatest Italian poet of the 19th century and a central figure of Romanticism.

alessandro-manzoni.name: Alessandro Manzoni
alessandro-manzoni.summary: An Italian philosopher, poet and novelist (1785-1873) best known for The Betrothed (1827), a milestone that helped unify the modern Italian language and symbolized Italy's unification movement.

anna-maria-mozzoni.name: Anna Maria Mozzoni
anna-maria-mozzoni.summary: Italian activist (1837–1920) regarded as founder of Italy's women's movement, known for her role in gaining women's suffrage there.

il-conciliatore.name: Il Conciliatore
il-conciliatore.summary: A progressive Milanese literary and scientific journal (1818–1819), influential in the early Italian Risorgimento, shut down by Austrian censors.

silvio-pellico.name: Silvio Pellico
silvio-pellico.summary: Italian writer, poet and patriot, 1789–1854, active in Italian unification and best remembered for his memoir My Prisons.

ludovico-di-breme.name: Ludovico di Breme
ludovico-di-breme.summary: Italian writer and thinker (1780–1820) who contributed to Milan's leading Romantic journal, Il Conciliatore.

giovanni-berchet.name: Giovanni Berchet
giovanni-berchet.summary: Italian poet and patriot (1783–1851) who wrote an influential manifesto on Italian Romanticism and took part in the nationalist revolutions of 1821 and 1848.

alaide-gualberta-beccari.name: Alaide Gualberta Beccari
alaide-gualberta-beccari.summary: Italian feminist, republican and social reformer (1842–1906) who published the feminist journal Woman during the 1870s and 1880s.

john-stuart-mill.name: John Stuart Mill
john-stuart-mill.summary: English philosopher and politician (1806–1873), a leading liberal thinker who championed individual liberty, women's rights and utilitarianism, author of On Liberty.

the-subjection-of-women.name: The Subjection of Women
the-subjection-of-women.summary: 1869 essay by John Stuart Mill, developed with his wife Harriet Taylor Mill, arguing for equality between the sexes at a time this defied conventional norms.

giuseppe-acerbi.name: Giuseppe Acerbi
giuseppe-acerbi.summary: An Italian naturalist, explorer and composer (1773–1846).

camillo-golgi.name: Camillo Golgi
camillo-golgi.summary: Italian biologist who won the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, shared with Santiago Ramón y Cajal, for work on the nervous system, after discovering the black reaction staining method in 1873.

santiago-ram-n-y-cajal.name: Santiago Ramón y Cajal
santiago-ram-n-y-cajal.summary: Spanish neuroscientist and histologist (1852–1934) who pioneered modern neuroscience and shared the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Camillo Golgi for work on the nervous system's structure.

alessandro-volta.name: Alessandro Volta
alessandro-volta.summary: An Italian physicist and chemist (1745-1827) who invented the electric battery, the voltaic pile, in 1799, proving electricity could be generated chemically and founding the field of electrochemistry.

voltaic-pile.name: Voltaic pile
voltaic-pile.summary: The first electrical battery able to provide continuous current, invented by Alessandro Volta and published in 1799, enabling discoveries like water electrolysis and several new chemical elements.

isaac-peral.name: Isaac Peral
isaac-peral.summary: Spanish naval engineer (1851–1895) who designed the Peral, the first electric-powered submarine, launched in 1888.

guglielmo-marconi.name: Guglielmo Marconi
guglielmo-marconi.summary: An Italian engineer (1874–1937) credited as the inventor of radio for his wireless telegraph system, sharing the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics with Ferdinand Braun.

k-ferdinand-braun.name: Ferdinand Braun
k-ferdinand-braun.summary: German physicist (1850–1918) who shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics with Marconi for developing radio, and built the first cathode-ray tube, later leading to television.

bristol-channel.name: Bristol Channel
bristol-channel.summary: Major inlet of the sea separating South Wales from South West England, extending from the Severn Estuary out to the North Atlantic Ocean.

golgi-s-method.name: Black reaction
golgi-s-method.summary: Original name Camillo Golgi gave in 1873 to his silver staining technique for viewing nervous tissue, later known as Golgi's method or the Golgi stain.

abbiategrasso.name: Abbiategrasso
abbiategrasso.summary: A town in the Po valley of Lombardy, northern Italy, about 22 kilometres from Milan.

stanislao-cannizzaro.name: Stanislao Cannizzaro
stanislao-cannizzaro.summary: Italian chemist (1826–1910) known for the Cannizzaro reaction and his influential role at the 1860 Karlsruhe Congress on atomic weights.

amedeo-avogadro.name: Amedeo Avogadro
amedeo-avogadro.summary: Italian scientist (1776–1856) who proposed that equal volumes of gases under the same conditions contain equal numbers of molecules, now called Avogadro's law.

copley-medal.name: Copley Medal
copley-medal.summary: The most prestigious award of the UK's Royal Society for outstanding scientific achievement, first given in 1731 and considered a forerunner of the Nobel Prize.

avogadro-s-law.name: Avogadro's law
avogadro-s-law.summary: A gas law stating that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules, proposed by Amedeo Avogadro in 1811.

victor-emmanuel-iii.name: Victor Emmanuel III
victor-emmanuel-iii.summary: King of Italy from 1900 until his abdication in 1946, who also briefly held the titles Emperor of Ethiopia and King of the Albanians; his reign spanned both World Wars and the Fascist era.

antonio-meucci.name: Antonio Meucci
antonio-meucci.summary: Italian inventor (1808–1889) who built an early voice-communication device that some credit as the first telephone, though Alexander Graham Bell received the 1876 patent.

alexander-graham-bell.name: Alexander Graham Bell
alexander-graham-bell.summary: A Scottish-born Canadian-American inventor and scientist (1847-1922) credited with patenting the first practical telephone in 1876 and co-founding AT&T in 1885.

loop-of-henle.name: Loop of Henle
loop-of-henle.summary: A part of the kidney's nephron, named after its discoverer Friedrich Gustav Jakob Henle, that creates a concentration gradient enabling water reabsorption and concentrated urine.

jagadish-chandra-bose.name: Jagadish Chandra Bose
jagadish-chandra-bose.summary: Indian polymath (1858–1937) who pioneered radio microwave research, contributed to botany, founded the Bose Institute, and is considered the father of Bengali science fiction.

coherer.name: coherer
coherer.summary: An early radio signal detector used in the first wireless telegraphy receivers around 1900, based on 1890 findings by physicist Édouard Branly.

kingdom-of-sardinia.name: Kingdom of Sardinia
kingdom-of-sardinia.summary: A Southern European kingdom from the late 1200s to mid-1800s, first held by the Crown of Aragon and Spain from 1324 and then by the House of Savoy from 1720.

kingdom-of-naples.name: Kingdom of Naples
kingdom-of-naples.summary: A state ruling southern Italy from 1282 to 1816, formed after the War of the Sicilian Vespers and later contested by France and Spain before coming under Spanish control by 1504.

kingdom-of-the-two-sicilies.name: Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
kingdom-of-the-two-sicilies.summary: A kingdom in southern Italy from 1816 to 1861 formed by merging the Kingdom of Sicily and Kingdom of Naples, ruled by the House of Bourbon-Two Sicilies until overthrown by Giuseppe Garibaldi in 1860.

iron-crown.name: Iron Crown
iron-crown.summary: A medieval reliquary crown of gold and jewels around a central band traditionally said to be forged from a nail of the True Cross, used to crown some Holy Roman Emperors as kings of Italy.

milan-cathedral.name: Milan Cathedral
milan-cathedral.summary: The cathedral church of Milan, Italy, dedicated to the Nativity of St. Mary; construction began in 1386 and finished in 1965, making it the largest church in Italy.

camillo-benso-count-of-cavour.name: Count Camillo Benso di Cavour
camillo-benso-count-of-cavour.summary: Italian statesman and Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Sardinia from 1852, a key architect of Italian unification who briefly became Italy's first prime minister before his death in 1861.

house-of-savoy.name: House of Savoy
house-of-savoy.summary: A royal dynasty established in 1003 that expanded from the Alpine County of Savoy to rule Sicily, Sardinia and eventually the unified Kingdom of Italy until 1946.

giovanni-giolitti.name: Giovanni Giolitti
giovanni-giolitti.summary: Italian statesman (1842–1928) who served as prime minister five times between 1892 and 1921, known for the coalition tactic of "trasformismo" and progressive social reforms.

boxer-rebellion.name: Boxer Rebellion
boxer-rebellion.summary: An anti-foreign, anti-Christian uprising in North China (1899–1901) by the "Boxers," a martial-arts movement, ultimately defeated by an alliance of eight foreign powers.

italian-idealism.name: Italian idealism
italian-idealism.summary: A philosophical movement in Italy shaped by German idealism, especially Hegel, growing out of 19th-century Risorgimento spiritualism and culminating with Benedetto Croce and Giovanni Gentile.

ren-descartes.name: René Descartes
ren-descartes.summary: A French philosopher, mathematician and scientist (1596–1650) known for "I think, therefore I am" and for founding analytic geometry.

immanuel-kant.name: Immanuel Kant
immanuel-kant.summary: German Enlightenment philosopher (1724–1804) whose work on knowledge, ethics and metaphysics, especially the Critique of Pure Reason, made him among the most influential thinkers in Western philosophy.

georg-wilhelm-friedrich-hegel.name: Hegel
georg-wilhelm-friedrich-hegel.summary: German philosopher (1770–1831) and major figure in German idealism, whose dialectical system, 'absolute idealism,' shaped modern metaphysics, political philosophy and philosophy of religion.

antonio-rosmini.name: Antonio Rosmini
antonio-rosmini.summary: Italian Catholic priest and philosopher (1797–1855) who founded the Rosminians and pioneered concepts of social justice and Italian Liberal Catholicism; later beatified.

vincenzo-gioberti.name: Vincenzo Gioberti
vincenzo-gioberti.summary: Italian Catholic priest, philosopher and politician (1801–1852) who served as Prime Minister of Sardinia from 1848 to 1849 and was a prominent voice for liberal Catholicism.

augusto-vera.name: Augusto Vera
augusto-vera.summary: Italian philosopher (1813–1885) who followed and translated Hegel's works.

bertrando-spaventa.name: Bertrando Spaventa
bertrando-spaventa.summary: Leading Italian philosopher (1817-1883) whose ideas influenced the unification of Italy and philosophical thought in the 20th century.

francesco-de-sanctis.name: Francesco De Sanctis
francesco-de-sanctis.summary: Italian literary critic, scholar and politician (1817–1883), a leading historian of Italian language and literature during the 19th century.

pasquale-villari.name: Pasquale Villari
pasquale-villari.summary: An Italian historian and politician (1827-1917), many of whose works were translated into English by his wife.

ontologism.name: Ontologism
ontologism.summary: Philosophical system, mainly linked to Nicolas Malebranche, holding that God and divine ideas are the first objects known by the intellect; condemned by the Holy Office in 1861.

giovanni-gentile.name: Giovanni Gentile
giovanni-gentile.summary: Italian philosopher and politician (1875–1944), a leading figure of Italian idealism known for "actualism" and self-described "philosopher of fascism"; assassinated by partisans in 1944.

gaetano-sanseverino.name: Gaetano Sanseverino
gaetano-sanseverino.summary: Italian philosopher and theologian (1811–1865) who made a comparative study of the scholastics, especially Thomas Aquinas, and their connection to the teachings of the Church Fathers.

joseph-kleutgen.name: Joseph Kleutgen
joseph-kleutgen.summary: German Jesuit theologian and philosopher (1811–1883) who contributed significantly to the establishment of Neo-scholasticism.

neo-scholasticism.name: Neo-scholasticism
neo-scholasticism.summary: A revival and development of medieval Scholasticism in Catholic theology, also called neo-scholastic Thomism for its debt to Thomas Aquinas, beginning in the late 19th century.

benedetto-croce.name: Benedetto Croce
benedetto-croce.summary: Italian idealist philosopher, historian and politician (1866–1952) who influenced Italian intellectuals from Marxists to fascists and led the Italian Liberal Party.

thomas-aquinas.name: Thomas Aquinas
thomas-aquinas.summary: An Italian Dominican friar, theologian and philosopher (c. 1225–1274) who blended Aristotelian philosophy with Christian doctrine and founded the school of thought called Thomism.

golasecca.name: Golasecca
golasecca.summary: Town in the province of Varese, Lombardy, Italy, that lent its name to the prehistoric Golasecca culture after graves were excavated there in 1822.

battle-of-ticinus.name: Battle of Ticinus
battle-of-ticinus.summary: A cavalry battle fought in November 218 BC between Hannibal's Carthaginian forces and a Roman army under Publius Cornelius Scipio, part of the opening moves of the Second Punic War.

hannibal.name: Hannibal
hannibal.summary: A Carthaginian general (247–183/181 BC) who led forces against Rome in the Second Punic War, famously crossing the Alps with war elephants to invade Italy.

scipio-africanus.name: Scipio Africanus
scipio-africanus.summary: Roman general (236/235-c.183 BC) who defeated Hannibal at the Battle of Zama in 202 BC, ending the Second Punic War and earning him the epithet 'Africanus'.

vittorio-calcina.name: Vittorio Calcina
vittorio-calcina.summary: Italian filmmaker, regarded as the first in Italian history. He lived from 31 December 1847 to 31 December 1916.

pope-leo-xiii.name: Pope Leo XIII
pope-leo-xiii.summary: Head of the Catholic Church from 1878 to 1903, called the "Pope of the Workers" for his 1891 encyclical on workers' rights and known for reviving the philosophy of Thomas Aquinas.

lumi-re-brothers.name: Lumière brothers
lumi-re-brothers.summary: French photography equipment makers Auguste (1862–1954) and Louis (1864–1948), among the earliest filmmakers. Their first paid public screening, on 28 December 1895, is traditionally seen as the birth of cinema.

gabriel-de-mortillet.name: Gabriel de Mortillet
gabriel-de-mortillet.summary: French archaeologist and anthropologist (1821–1898), born at Meylan, Isère.

golasecca-culture.name: Golasecca culture
golasecca-culture.summary: Late Bronze Age and Early Iron Age culture (9th–4th centuries BC) in northern Italy, named for its type-site near Golasecca and spread across a wide area south of the Alps.

national-archaeological-museum-france.name: Musée des Antiquités Nationales
national-archaeological-museum-france.summary: A major French archaeology museum covering prehistoric times to the Merovingian period (450–750), housed in the Château de Saint-Germain-en-Laye near Paris; this was its earlier name.

rerum-novarum.name: Rerum novarum
rerum-novarum.summary: Open letter issued by Pope Leo XIII on 15 May 1891 to Catholic bishops about the working class. It backed trade unions and a living wage while rejecting both state socialism and laissez-faire capitalism.

alexandre-bertrand.name: Alexandre Bertrand
alexandre-bertrand.summary: French archaeologist born in Rennes in 1820, who died in 1902.

giovanni-pastrone.name: Giovanni Pastrone
giovanni-pastrone.summary: Italian silent-film pioneer (1883-1959), also called Piero Fosco. His film Cabiria influenced directors such as D. W. Griffith, and Martin Scorsese credits him with inventing the epic movie.
